blocks.text: 1. Encoder-Decoder Attention
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881279-138973528.png

Why Attention, the previous topic, motivated letting the decoder look back at every input position directly. Encoder-Decoder Attention is the first concrete application of this idea, explored throughout this topic.
It lets the decoder genuinely attend to the encoder's own outputs at every single output step, a genuinely concrete, mathematical mechanism covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping Direct Access

This connects back to direct access to all positions, already covered in Why Attention. Every single encoder position's own output genuinely stays available, already covered there, as the foundation this topic builds on.
Encoder-Decoder Attention genuinely puts that direct access into concrete, mathematical practice, turning the previous topic's own conceptual motivation into a genuinely working mechanism.
3. Where This Fits In The Architecture

blocks.alt: Where This Fits In The Architecture
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881279-607292791.png

This connects back to the decoder's own role, already covered in Encoder-Decoder Architecture. At each decoder time step, before generating the next output word, it genuinely attends to the encoder's own outputs first.
This is a genuinely new step inserted directly into the decoding process already covered there, adding attention as a genuinely additional stage before the decoder produces its own next prediction.
4. Computing Relevance Scores
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881281-964194930.png
The genuinely core computation compares the decoder's own current state against every single encoder position, a genuinely direct, pairwise comparison across the entire input.

This produces a genuinely relevance score for each encoder position, covered in mathematical detail in the very next topic of this module, quantifying exactly how relevant each input position currently is.

blocks.text: 5. Turning Scores Into Weights
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881281-903818791.png

This connects back to Softmax, already covered in the Activation Functions module. Those genuinely raw relevance scores genuinely get passed through Softmax, directly reusing that earlier activation function.
This produces attention weights that genuinely sum to exactly 1 across all encoder positions, giving a genuinely proper, interpretable probability distribution over the entire input.
6. The Weighted Sum Computation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881281-920972106.png
This connects back to the weighted sum, already covered in the Convolution Operation. Multiply each encoder position's own output by its own attention weight, then genuinely sum everything together.
This produces a genuinely dynamic context vector, different at every single decoder time step, a genuinely direct extension of the weighted sum idea already covered in that earlier module.

blocks.content: This dynamic context vector, already covered in this topic, is computed fresh at every single decoder time step, genuinely different each time depending on what the decoder currently needs to focus on.

blocks.text: 7. Dynamic Context Versus A Fixed Vector

blocks.alt: Dynamic Context Versus A Fixed Vector
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881281-587328029.png

This connects back to the context vector, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. Unlike that earlier, genuinely single, fixed context vector, this genuinely new context vector changes at every decoder step.
This directly delivers the flexibility already covered as this entire module's own core motivation, replacing one static summary with a genuinely dynamic, per-step computation.

blocks.text: 8. A Valuable Interpretability Benefit

A genuinely valuable side benefit connects back to visualizing feature maps, already covered in Feature Maps. Attention weights genuinely reveal exactly which input positions the decoder focused on for each output word.
This gives a genuinely direct, visual window into the model's own internal reasoning, similar in spirit to the visualization technique already covered for feature maps in that earlier topic.
9. Recognizing When Encoder-Decoder Attention Is Genuinely Valuable

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Encoder-Decoder Attention Is Genuinely Valuable
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445881752-530452249.png

This connects back to Machine Translation, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. Attending to genuinely different source words per target word, already covered in this topic, directly improves translation quality.
Wanting genuinely interpretable insight into what a model actually focused on is another genuine case where attention weights, already covered, directly provide exactly that visibility.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates computing attention weights and a dynamic context vector for a single decoder step, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 5
hidden_size = 4

encoder_outputs = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))  # already covered as direct access to all positions
decoder_state = rng.normal(size=hidden_size)  # the decoder's own current state, already covered in this topic

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum()

# already covered as computing relevance scores in this topic
relevance_scores = np.array([np.dot(decoder_state, enc_out) for enc_out in encoder_outputs])
attention_weights = softmax(relevance_scores)  # already covered as turning scores into weights in this topic

# already covered as the weighted sum computation in this topic
dynamic_context_vector = sum(w * enc_out for w, enc_out in zip(attention_weights, encoder_outputs))

print("Attention weights (sum to 1, already covered in this topic):", np.round(attention_weights, 3))
print("Sum check:", round(attention_weights.sum(), 6))
print(f"\nDynamic context vector shape: {dynamic_context_vector.shape}")
print(f"Most attended encoder position: {np.argmax(attention_weights)}, already covered as interpretability in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Encoder-Decoder Attention lets the decoder attend to the encoder's outputs at every step.
It puts the direct access already motivated in Why Attention into concrete practice.
At each decoder step, it attends to encoder outputs before generating the next word.
It computes a relevance score for each encoder position by comparing it to the decoder state.
Softmax turns those raw scores into attention weights that sum to exactly 1.
A weighted sum of encoder outputs, using those weights, produces a dynamic context vector.
This context vector changes at every decoder step, unlike a single, fixed context vector.
Attention weights offer a valuable interpretability benefit, revealing what the model focused on.
